1.meaningEn: Saying your name when introducing yourself

examples.en: Hello. I am Minsu.
Hello. I am Sarah.

grammar.noteEn: ___ is for your name.

examples.en: I am Korean.
I am American.

grammar.noteEn: ___ is for a country name.

examples.en: I am a student.
I am an office worker.

grammar.noteEn: ___ is for your job or role.

examples.en: How much is this?
How much is coffee?

grammar.noteEn: ___ is for the item.

examples.en: I'll have an iced coffee.
I'll have a sandwich.

grammar.noteEn: ___ is for the item or menu.

examples.en: Where is the restroom?
Where is the exit?

grammar.noteEn: ___ is for the place.

examples.en: My name is Minji.
My name is Emily.

grammar.noteEn: Fill ___ with your name

1.meaningEn: Asking someone to speak more slowly

examples.text: 한국어 좀 더 천천히 말해 주세요.
examples.ko: 한국어 좀 더 천천히 말해 주세요.
examples.en: Please speak Korean more slowly.

examples.text: 이 부분 좀 더 천천히 말해 주세요.
examples.ko: 이 부분 좀 더 천천히 말해 주세요.
examples.en: Please say this part more slowly.

grammar.noteEn: Fill ___ with language or topic

examples.text: 이름 다시 한 번 말해 주세요.
examples.ko: 이름 다시 한 번 말해 주세요.
examples.en: Please say your name again.

examples.text: 금액 다시 한 번 말해 주세요.
examples.ko: 금액 다시 한 번 말해 주세요.
examples.en: Please say the amount again.

grammar.noteEn: Fill ___ with what you want repeated

examples.en: Where is the restroom?
Where is the station?

grammar.noteEn: Fill ___ with the place you want to find

examples.en: Shall we meet at the cafe?
Shall we meet at the park?

grammar.noteEn: The blank is the meeting place.

examples.en: Let's meet at two o'clock.
Let's meet at four o'clock.

grammar.noteEn: The blank is the meeting time.

2.meaningEn: Saying what you want to do

examples.en: I want to go shopping.
I want to go hiking.

grammar.noteEn: The blank is the action you want to do.

examples.en: I will exercise.
I will study.

grammar.noteEn: The blank is the planned action.

examples.en: Please let me off at Myeongdong.
Please let me off at Seoul Station.

grammar.noteEn: The blank is the destination.

2.meaningEn: Asking for another size or color

examples.en: Do you have a bigger size?
Do you have this in blue?

grammar.noteEn: The blank is the color or size.

2.meaningKo: 다른 색깔이나 사이즈 보여 달라고 요청하기
2.meaningEn: Asking to see a different size or color

examples.en: Please show me the black one.
Please show me the small size.

grammar.noteEn: The blank is the color or size.

examples.en: Please give me cold medicine.
Please give me headache medicine.

grammar.noteEn: The blank is the name of the medicine.

examples.en: This scene is really funny!
You’re really awesome!

grammar.noteKo: 첫 번째 빈칸은 대상, 두 번째 빈칸은 감탄 형용사/동사
grammar.noteEn: First blank: subject, second blank: exclamatory verb/adjective

3.meaningKo: 드라마, 노래, 프로그램에 대해 의견 묻기
3.meaningEn: Asking for an opinion about a drama, song, or show

examples.text: 그 드라마 결말에 대해서 어떻게 생각해?
examples.ko: 그 드라마 결말에 대해서 어떻게 생각해?
examples.en: What do you think about the ending of that drama?
What do you think about this song?

grammar.noteEn: Put the topic in the blank

3.meaningEn: Requesting an exchange for a purchased item

examples.en: Please exchange these shoes.
Please exchange the size.

grammar.noteEn: Put the item you want to exchange in the blank

3.meaningEn: Sharing your opinion casually with a friend

examples.en: The drama I watched yesterday was really fun.
This song was really fun.

grammar.noteEn: Put what you are talking about in the blank

3.meaningEn: Politely asking someone to help with a problem

examples.en: Can you help me with this?
Can you help me with my homework?

grammar.noteEn: Put what you need help with in the blank

3.meaningEn: Explaining why you couldn't do something

examples.en: I couldn't do it because of a cold.
I couldn't do it because of work.

grammar.noteEn: Fill the blank with the reason

examples.en: Here's what I think about the ending.

examples.text: 저는 이 노래에 대해 이렇게 생각해요.
examples.ko: 저는 이 노래에 대해 어떻게 생각해요.
examples.en: Here's what I think about this song.

grammar.noteEn: Put the topic in the blank

3.meaningEn: Saying what will happen if they do that

examples.en: If you leave now, you will be late.
It would be good if you rest tomorrow.

grammar.noteKo: 앞 빈칸은 조건이고, 뒤 빈칸은 그때의 결과다.
grammar.noteEn: The first blank is the condition and the second is the result.

4.meaningEn: Speak politely to a manager or superior

examples.en: The team leader started the meeting.
The department head left early today.

grammar.noteKo: 첫 번째 빈칸에는 높임의 대상을, 두 번째 빈칸에는 높임 동사를 넣음.
grammar.noteEn: First blank: honorific subject, second blank: honorific verb.

4.meaningEn: Discuss a news topic and give a balanced opinion

examples.text: 새로운 정책에 대해서는 아직 잘 모르겠다는 생각이에요.
examples.ko: 새로운 정책에 대해서는 아직 잘 모르겠다는 생각이에요.
examples.en: Regarding the new policy, I think I'm not sure yet.
About working from home, I think there are pros and cons.

grammar.noteKo: 첫 번째 빈칸은 주제, 두 번째 빈칸은 자신의 의견.
grammar.noteEn: First blank: topic, second blank: your opinion.

examples.en: I can't go today. I have plans.

examples.text: 지금 나가야 돼요. 택시가 기다리고 있거든요.
examples.ko: 지금 나가야 돼요. 택시가 기다리고 있거든요.
examples.en: I have to leave now. The taxi is waiting.

grammar.noteKo: 이유나 상황을 자연스럽게 설명할 때 사용
grammar.noteEn: Used for explaining reasons in a conversational way

examples.en: We talked about it yesterday, remember?
It's too expensive, as you know.

grammar.noteKo: 이미 알고 있는 사실을 상대방에게 상기시킴
grammar.noteEn: Used to point out something both people already know

4.meaningEn: Politely asking a manager to check something

examples.en: Could you please check the report?
Could you please check the schedule?

grammar.noteEn: Put what you want checked in the blank

examples.text: 보고서 작성 좀 도와주실 수 있으세요?
examples.ko: 보고서 작성 좀 도와주실 수 있으세요?
examples.en: Could you please help me with the report?

examples.text: 오늘 일정 조율 좀 도와주실 수 있으세요?
examples.ko: 오늘 일정 조율 좀 도와주실 수 있으세요?
examples.en: Could you please help me coordinate today's schedule?

grammar.noteKo: 도움을 받고 싶은 대상을 높여서 사용하는 표현
grammar.noteEn: The blank is what you want help with.

examples.en: Could you please check the report for me?

examples.text: 내일 일정 조정 좀 부탁드려도 될까요?
examples.ko: 내일 일정 조정 좀 부탁드려도 될까요?
examples.en: Could you help adjust tomorrow’s schedule?

grammar.noteKo: 첫 번째 ___에 정중하게 부탁하는 내용을 넣음
grammar.noteEn: The blank is for what you are requesting

examples.en: I would appreciate it if you could help me with the report.
I would appreciate it if you could help prepare for the meeting.

grammar.noteEn: The blank is for the thing you are asking help with.

5.meaningEn: Introducing a meme or slang to a friend

examples.text: 지난주 예능 봤어, 혹시 ‘소주 한 잔’이라고 들어봤어?
examples.ko: 지난주 예능 봤어, 혹시 ‘소주 한 잔’이라고 들어봤어?
examples.en: Did you see last week's variety show? Have you heard of 'Soju Han Jan'?
Have you been on the internet lately? Have you heard of 'Jjalbang'?

grammar.noteKo: 첫 번째 ___에 상황, 두 번째 ___에 밈/유행어.
grammar.noteEn: First blank is situation/context, second is meme or phrase.

5.pattern: ___라고 하면 좀 그렇고, ___라고 해야 할 것 같아요.
5.meaningEn: Switching between levels of formality or expressions

examples.text: 반말이라고 하면 좀 그렇고, 존댓말이라고 해야 할 것 같아요.
examples.ko: 반말이라고 하면 좀 그렇고, 존댓말이라고 해야 할 것 같아요.
examples.en: It feels off to say it's informal speech, I think I should call it polite speech.

examples.text: 친구라고 하면 좀 그렇고, 선배라고 해야 할 것 같아요.
examples.ko: 친구라고 하면 좀 그렇고, 선배라고 해야 할 것 같아요.
examples.en: To call them a friend doesn't feel right, I think I should say 'senior.'

grammar.noteKo: 첫 번째 ___에 들어가는 말을 완곡하게 설명할 때
grammar.noteEn: First ___ is what you could call it

grammar.noteKo: 두 번째 ___에 더 적합한 말을 넣음
grammar.noteEn: Second ___ is what you choose to call it

quiz.prompt: ___라고 하면 좀 그렇고, 선배라고 해야 할 것 같아요.

5.meaningEn: Explaining a cultural reference or phrase

examples.text: 복세편살이라는 건 예능에서 자주 나오는 표현이야.
examples.ko: 복세편살이라는 건 예능에서 자주 나오는 표현이야.
examples.en: The phrase 'boksepyunsal' is something you often hear in variety shows.

examples.text: 무야호라는 건 밈에서 자주 나오는 표현이야.
examples.ko: 무야호라는 건 밈에서 자주 나오는 표현이야.
examples.en: The phrase 'muyaho' is a common meme expression.

grammar.noteKo: 첫 번째 ___에 설명할 표현, 두 번째 ___에 출처나 맥락을 넣음
grammar.noteEn: First ___ is the phrase, second ___ is the context/source

examples.en: It's okay to cry when things are tough.
It's okay to rest when you're having a hard time.

grammar.noteEn: The blank is an action that comforts.

examples.text: 나 같아도 그만두는 거 힘들었을 것 같아.
examples.ko: 나 같아도 그만두는 거 힘들었을 것 같아.
examples.en: If it were me, quitting would have been hard too.

examples.text: 나 같아도 참는 거 힘들었을 것 같아.
examples.ko: 나 같아도 참는 거 힘들었을 것 같아.
examples.en: If it were me, enduring it would have been tough too.

grammar.noteEn: The blank is a situation or action.

examples.text: 이번에는 주말 출근이 어려울 것 같습니다.
examples.ko: 이번에는 주말 출근이 어려울 것 같습니다.
examples.en: This time, working on the weekend will be difficult for me.

examples.text: 이번에는 추가 업무가 어려울 것 같습니다.
examples.ko: 이번에는 추가 업무가 어려울 것 같습니다.
examples.en: This time, taking on extra work will be difficult for me.

grammar.noteKo: ___ 자리에 들어가는 내용을 완곡하게 말할 때 사용
grammar.noteEn: ___ slot is for the action being declined

5.pattern: 너무 ___하지 마. 네가 얼마나 노력했는지 알아.

examples.text: 너무 속상해하지 마. 네가 얼마나 노력했는지 알아.
examples.ko: 너무 속상해하지 마. 네가 얼마나 노력했는지 알아.
examples.en: Don't be too upset. I know how hard you tried.

examples.text: 너무 자책하지 마. 네가 얼마나 노력했는지 알아.
examples.ko: 너무 자책하지 마. 네가 얼마나 노력했는지 알아.
examples.en: Don't blame yourself too much. I know how much effort you put in.

grammar.noteKo: ___ 자리에 위로하고 싶은 감정이나 행동을 넣음
grammar.noteEn: ___ slot is the feeling or action

quiz.prompt: 너무 ___하지 마. 네가 얼마나 노력했는지 알아.

5.meaningEn: Praising someone for improving the mood

examples.en: Thanks to you, senior, the mood has really improved.
Thanks to you, manager, the atmosphere got much better.

grammar.noteKo: ___ 자리에 분위기를 좋게 만든 사람을 넣음
grammar.noteEn: ___ is the person who improved the mood
